issue.title: painterSortStable is not stable with invisible objects (Chrome)
Artifacting/Flickering Model
issue.body:
Having an issue with my models.

Here is the model, it looks pretty good, but it flickers in the animation loop, and looks progressively worse (flickers more, gets more patchy) as you zoom away from the model.
http://i.imgur.com/lfB8uDw.png

Then I tried scaling the model \* 100 to switch from m to cm (to match other units), and I get this:
http://i.imgur.com/zDtuO7V.png

I'm thinking the flickering (obv not shown by these static images) might be related, any ideas what would cause this sort of artifacting?

Edit: Running chrome 24.0.1312.56
Edit 2: Using Canvas as opposed to WebGL seems to fix it, but obviously that is much slower, hope that gives a hint?

issue.title: painterSortStable not actually stable
issue.body: Had to disable sortObjects to prevent transparent faces randomly flickering on Chrome (Issue is not actually apparent on Safari). It seems to be related to the sorting not being coherent across multiple frames (GeometryGroups draw order is random within the same Geometry). This issue is most obvious when use MeshFaceMaterial.

body: Part of the bugfix (the change to WebGLRenderer) was removed in a28e942faf02c556279f31ba333030dafc32abc5 (see https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/commit/a28e942faf02c556279f31ba333030dafc32abc5#L1L416). The bug is still present in the WebGLRenderer of r57.

issue.title: Sorting of objects not stable (Chrome)
issue.body:
(Rev 57)

This is related to https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/issues/2966, but this correction is not enough in Chrome.

In the renderList list, some objects can have undefined values for the z value used for sorting (webglObject.z), which leads to unstable sorting under Chrome (with Firefox and Safari, it appears that webglObject.z is never undefined, so the sorting is ok...).

Setting webglObject.z=0; just after webglObject.id=i; fixes the problem.

Another fix would be to sort only objects that need to be sorted (the ones that have webglObject.render = true) and not the whole renderList list (that may be a performance boost too), in which case all objects would have a valid z value.
